@dev Contract module that allows children to implement role-based access
 control mechanisms. This is a lightweight version that doesn't allow enumerating role
 members except through off-chain means by accessing the contract event logs. Some
 applications may benefit from on-chain enumerability, for those cases see
 {AccessControlEnumerable}.
 Roles are referred to by their `bytes32` identifier. These should be exposed
 in the external API and be unique. The best way to achieve this is by
 using `public constant` hash digests:
 ```solidity
 bytes32 public constant MY_ROLE = keccak256("MY_ROLE");
 ```
 Roles can be used to represent a set of permissions. To restrict access to a
 function call, use {hasRole}:
 ```solidity
 function foo() public {
     require(hasRole(MY_ROLE, msg.sender));
     ...
 }
 ```
 Roles can be granted and revoked dynamically via the {grantRole} and
 {revokeRole} functions. Each role has an associated admin role, and only
 accounts that have a role's admin role can call {grantRole} and {revokeRole}.
 By default, the admin role for all roles is `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which means
 that only accounts with this role will be able to grant or revoke other
 roles. More complex role relationships can be created by using
 {_setRoleAdmin}.
 WARNING: The `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is also its own admin: it has permission to
 grant and revoke this role. Extra precautions should be taken to secure
 accounts that have been granted it. We recommend using {AccessControlDefaultAdminRules}
 to enforce additional security measures for this role.

@dev Modifier that checks that an account has a specific role. Reverts
 with an {AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount} error including the required role.
@inheritdoc ERC165

@dev Reverts with an {AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount} error if `_msgSender()`

@dev Revokes `role` from `account`.
 If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event.
 Requirements:
 - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.
 May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

@dev Revokes `role` from the calling account.
 Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's
 purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges
 if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced).
 If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked}
 event.
 Requirements:
 - the caller must be `callerConfirmation`.
 May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

@dev Sets `adminRole` as ``role``'s admin role.

@dev Provides information about the current execution context, including the
 sender of the transaction and its data. While these are generally available
 via msg.sender and msg.data, they should not be accessed in such a direct
 manner, since when dealing with meta-transactions the account sending and
 paying for execution may not be the actual sender (as far as an application
 is concerned).
 This contract is only required for intermediate, library-like contracts.

 For an implementation, see {ERC165}.

@title CorrelationDecision
 @dev Two-step, attested correlation.
  1. The federated-correlation service (CORRELATOR_ROLE) submits the result commitment,
     confidence class, algorithm version and the affected domains.
  2. Affected domains attest the SAME result hash (after checking it against their own
     off-chain view). When attestations reach the governance quorum the result is recorded
     and the incident moves REGISTERED -> CORRELATED.
  A single (malicious) submitter can therefore no longer fix the correlation result.
  The correlator may re-submit while a result is still pending (new round, attestations reset).

@title DeviceRecovery
 @dev QUARANTINED -> RECOVERING -> ACTIVE | REVOKED with cross-domain validation.
  - The owning domain submits remediation / AI-evaluation / attestation / evidence commitments.
  - Other active domains validate; `requiredApprovals` approvals move the device to RECOVERING.
  - A validation window prevents a request from blocking a device forever (e.g. when
    requiredApprovals can never be reached): anyone can expire it after the window.
  - The designated verifier (set by the Security Authority) records the final assessment.
@dev Frees the device for a new request when validation could not complete in time.

@title DeviceRegistry
 @dev Device lifecycle: ACTIVE -> QUARANTINED -> RECOVERING -> ACTIVE | REVOKED.
  - quarantineDevice: the owning domain (local, immediate safety response) or the Security Authority.
  - applyDecision:    binds device state to a federation decision. If the proposal's target
                      resource is this device and the decision is QUARANTINE / REVOKE, any active
                      domain can apply it, so federation outcomes are enforceable on-chain.
  - revokeDevice:     Security Authority break-glass.
@dev Write-once wiring.
@dev Write-once wiring.
@dev Enforce a finalized federation decision (QUARANTINE or REVOKE) on its target device.
@dev Security Authority break-glass revocation.

@title DomainRegistry
 @dev Participating domains, roles, keys and status.
  - The Security Authority (SECAUTH_ROLE) is the single administrative root of the
    federation. Every other contract resolves "admin" through this registry, so the
    Security Authority can be a multisig / governance contract without touching other code.
  - validatorFlag is informational metadata. Actual BFT consensus membership is
    configured in the blockchain client (e.g. Besu QBFT validator set), not here.
  - CORRELATOR_ROLE identifies the federated-correlation / aggregation service that is
    allowed to submit correlation results (which affected domains then attest).
@dev Suspend / reactivate / remove. REMOVED is permanent.

@title ExecutionVerification
 @dev Peer verification of execution receipts.
  Receipt hashes reported by the responsible domain are attested by OTHER active domains.
  `requiredAttestations` approvals mark the action VERIFIED; the same number of rejections
  marks it FAILED (the responsible domain may then re-report with a new receipt).
  When every action of a plan is VERIFIED the incident moves EXECUTING -> VERIFIED.
  Closing (VERIFIED -> CLOSED) is an explicit step in IncidentRegistry.closeIncident,
  carrying a closure-record commitment.
  No single verifier account exists any more, so no single party can verify or block a plan.
  Note: requiredAttestations must not exceed the number of non-responsible active domains.
@dev Write-once wiring.
@dev Tally in VoteChoice order: [QUARANTINE, PATCH, REVOKE, MONITOR, NO_ACTION].

@title IncidentRegistry
 @dev On-chain incident state machine.
  REGISTERED -> CORRELATED -> RESPONSE_PROPOSED -> VOTING -> APPROVED -> EXECUTING
             -> VERIFIED -> CLOSED
  Exceptional paths (liveness):
    VOTING            -> CLOSED     federation explicitly voted NO_ACTION
    RESPONSE_PROPOSED / VOTING / EXECUTING / APPROVED -> ESCALATED
                                    (proposal expired, no quorum, execution stalled,
                                     approved-but-never-executed)
    ESCALATED         -> CORRELATED Security Authority re-opens for a new proposal
  Workflow-contract wiring is WRITE-ONCE: after setup nobody (including the Security
  Authority) can re-point a workflow address, so no single party can forge transitions.
@dev Approved by the federation but nobody created an execution plan.
@dev ESCALATED -> CORRELATED so a fresh proposal can be made.

@title ResponseDecision
 @dev Applies the governance rule F(V_1..V_n) to a finished vote.
  Outcomes:
   QUARANTINE / REVOKE / PATCH   threshold reached  -> proposal APPROVED, incident APPROVED
                                 (ties: higher vote count wins, then QUARANTINE > REVOKE > PATCH)
   MONITOR                       no threshold reached and MONITOR >= NO_ACTION votes -> APPROVED
   NO_ACTION                     no threshold reached and NO_ACTION > MONITOR votes
                                 -> proposal REJECTED, incident CLOSED (explicit federation decision)
   NO_QUORUM                     too few reveals -> proposal REJECTED, incident ESCALATED
                                 (an un-decided incident is never silently closed)

@dev Anyone may escalate a plan that missed its deadline: EXECUTING -> ESCALATED.

@title ResponseProposal
 @dev A response proposal for a CORRELATED incident.
  - Eligible voters are ALL currently-active affected domains (derived on-chain from the
    correlation result). The proposer can no longer hand-pick the electorate.
  - The proposer must itself be an affected domain.
  - At least one evidence commitment must exist for the incident.
  - actions: at least one primary action (QUARANTINE/PATCH/REVOKE/MONITOR); BLOCK_TRAFFIC is
    an additional action only. Voters choose the primary response; the winning primary
    action (plus the proposal's additional actions) is what may be executed.
  - A proposal can only EXPIRE if voting never started, and expiry escalates the incident
    instead of leaving it stuck.
@dev Write-once wiring.
@dev Write-once wiring.
